change.author: CarinaWolli

findings.title: Working-hours check rejects a slot if it is outside any one entry for that day, not all of them
findings.body:
`workingHours.find(...)` returns true (so the slot is rejected) as soon as one entry whose `days` includes the slot's day does not contain the slot. A host's `workingHours` routinely has several entries for the same day.

`getWorkingHours` splits any schedule that crosses UTC midnight into two entries: a same-day one and a shifted-days overflow entry (`packages/lib/availability.ts:101-121`). Example: a Mon–Fri 09:00–17:00 schedule in US Pacific (UTC-8) becomes 17:00–23:59 UTC on days 1–5 plus 00:00–01:00 UTC on days 2–6. For a Tuesday slot at 18:00Z the overflow entry is checked, `start < 0` is false, and `end (1080) > 60` is true, so the slot is rejected. For UTC+10 the mirror case rejects Mon–Thu.

The same happens with a schedule that has two ranges in one day (09–12 and 14–17): a 15:00 slot is rejected by the 09–12 entry.

This check now runs for every fixed host (lines 488-493) and every loose host (513-518). Any host whose local working day crosses UTC midnight, or who has split hours, loses most or all of their slots with no error. The existing tests use IST (UTC+5:30, no crossing, single range), so they do not catch it.

Fix: gather the entries whose `days` include the slot's day and reject only if none of them contains the slot, for example with `some` on a containment predicate. Decide separately whether a day with no entries at all should reject.

findings.title: `end` is computed identically to `start`, so the end of working hours is never really checked
findings.body: `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` duplicates `start`. The slot's end time (`slotEndTime`) is never compared with `workingHour.endTime`. The condition `end > workingHour.endTime` only rejects a slot that starts after the end. A 60-minute slot starting at 16:30 in a 09:00–17:00 window passes this check. Use `slotEndTime`, or state why only the start matters.

findings.title: Date-override check has the same any-entry problem, and ignores overrides that straddle UTC midnight
findings.body:
1) `dateOverrides.find` returns true on the first override on that date that does not contain the slot. If a host has two override ranges for one date (for example 09–12 and 14–17), a 15:00 slot is rejected by the first range. I did not check how the UI creates multiple ranges. Both ranges would be rows of `availability` with the same `date`, which `getUserAvailability` turns into separate `dateOverrides` entries (`packages/core/getUserAvailability.ts:215-224`).

2) The override is matched to a slot by comparing the UTC calendar date of the converted `date.start` with the slot's UTC date (lines 110-111). If the organizer's wall-clock window crosses UTC midnight (for example 09:00–17:00 at UTC+10 is 23:00Z the day before to 07:00Z), the part after midnight UTC is on a different date. `dateOverrideExist` stays false for those slots, so they fall through to the normal working-hours check and the override is ignored.

Suggested direction: reject only if no override range for that date contains the slot, and match by instant range rather than by date string.

findings.title: `===` on two Dayjs objects is always false
findings.body: `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares object references, so the branch never runs. It looks meant to handle a day-off override where start equals end. In that case a slot starting exactly at the override start is currently treated as available, because only `isAfter(end)` rejects it. Use `.isSame(...)`, or remove the branch.

findings.title: Shifted override minutes wrap at midnight; start/end can invert and the override then yields no slots
findings.body:
The shifted override is converted back to minutes-of-day with `.hour()*60 + .minute()`. If `offset` moves the window across midnight, the minutes wrap. For example, an organizer window of 15:00–21:00 with an invitee 6 h ahead becomes start=21:00 and end=03:00, so `startTime > endTime`. `buildSlots` drops it with `if (start >= end) continue` (line 68). The working hours for that user were already removed at lines 228-243, so the invitee sees no slots for that override. The shift also does not carry the day change: the `activeOverrides` filter (lines 206-208) still selects by the unshifted `override.start`. Clamp, or split the window at midnight, the way `getWorkingHours` does for overflow. Add a test with an offset that crosses midnight.

Smaller points: the shifted value is computed twice per bound, and `override.timeZone` is optional in the type (`packages/types/schedule.d.ts:5`), so `dayjs(...).tz(undefined)` falls back to the process timezone if a caller omits it.

findings.title: New test covers only a 30-minute offset shift on a single host
findings.body: The new case uses invitee +6:00 against the IST (+5:30) organizer, with a single host, a single override range and a non-midnight-crossing schedule. The PR is about fixed/round-robin hosts, working-hours checks and time zones, yet none of these is tested: no round-robin or collective scenario, no host with overflow working hours (for example UTC-8 or UTC+10), no split override ranges, and no invitee offset that moves an override across midnight. Tests for those would have caught the working-hours problem at `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:139`.

findings.title: `organizerTimeZone` is passed to the reserved-slot check but has no effect there
findings.body: This call passes no `dateOverrides` or `workingHours` (`availabilityCheckProps` holds only `eventLength` and `currentSeats`), and `busy` is built from selected slots. `organizerTimeZone` is read only inside the date-override branch, so the `userSchedule` lookup does nothing here. Remove the lookup and the argument, or pass the host's overrides and working hours if that was intended.

contracts.action: New working-hours check for each fixed and loose host inside checkIfIsAvailable
contracts.equivalent_path: getTimeSlots/getSlots in packages/lib/slots.ts already builds slots from aggregated working hours (getAggregateWorkingHours); the new check re-filters per host.
contracts.before_after: Before: slots came from aggregated working hours and were only filtered by busy times. After: each host's raw workingHours entries (UTC minutes, with midnight-overflow split entries and one entry per range) are also checked with `find`, which rejects on the first non-containing entry.
contracts.visible_effect: Hosts whose working day crosses UTC midnight, or who have split hours, lose slots on the booking page. There is no error or log.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent wrong result: valid slots are dropped.

contracts.action: Date-override time shift by invitee/organizer offset in getSlots
contracts.equivalent_path: Working-hours localisation at packages/lib/slots.ts:170-176, which converts to invitee-local minutes using getWorkingHours with the invitee utcOffset.
contracts.before_after: Before: override minutes were the organizer's wall-clock minutes taken as-is, so they were wrong for an invitee in another timezone. After: they are shifted by (inviteeOffset - organizerOffset), which is correct for same-day windows. Windows that cross midnight wrap by hour()/minute() and can invert.
contracts.visible_effect: Invitees in other timezones now see the override hours at the right local time, except for windows that cross midnight.
contracts.failure_mode: Inverted start/end is silently dropped by buildSlots (`start >= end`), so the override produces no slots.

contracts.action: Pass organizer timeZone through dateOverrides and into checkIfIsAvailable
contracts.equivalent_path: Existing getUserAvailability return value already includes `timeZone` (schedule?.timeZone || eventType?.timeZone || user.timeZone).
contracts.before_after: Before: overrides had no timezone. After: each override carries the host's timeZone, and each call site passes `schedule.timeZone`, `userSchedule.timeZone` or `userSchedule?.timeZone`.
contracts.visible_effect: Override conversion now uses the per-host timezone. The top-level organizerTimeZone for slot generation is still the event/first-host timezone.
contracts.failure_mode: The check uses the host's timezone but getSlots' buildSlots DST logic uses a single organizerTimeZone for all hosts. That is a mismatch for multi-timezone teams, but it was not introduced here.

summary: The new per-host working-hours check in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts` is wrong. It uses `find`, so it rejects a slot that is outside any single working-hours entry for that day. `getWorkingHours` splits schedules that cross UTC midnight into overflow entries, and schedules with split hours have several entries per day. Hosts like US Pacific or UTC+10 with 9–17 therefore lose most weekday slots silently; I rate this a blocker. The same check also computes `end` as a copy of `start`. The date-override check has the same any-range problem, a `===` on Dayjs objects that is always false, and date matching that misses overrides straddling UTC midnight. In `packages/lib/slots.ts`, the offset shift is right for same-day windows but wraps at midnight. The new test covers one 30-minute offset and one host only. I read all four files in full plus the callers and the working-hours builders. Nothing was run.
